findings.title: x3-quantum-crypto crate is an empty stub
findings.evidence: E020: src/ directory contains no .rs files. Declared as path dependency in runtime/Cargo.toml behind `pq` feature. crates/x3-pq/src/lib.rs exists but only declares types and a PQManager struct with empty body.
findings.impact: Post-quantum cryptography is advertised in docs (README mentions PQ as a roadmap item) but no implementation exists. Production builds cannot rely on `pq` feature. This is correctly excluded from WASM via #[cfg(feature = "pq")] guards but means PQ migration is research-only.
findings.recommendation: Either remove the empty crate and `pq` feature flag, or implement Dilithium/Falcon signing per x3-pq types. Do not advertise PQ support in user-facing docs until implemented and tested.
blocks: pq-experimental feature is correctly gated off in mainnet-rc1

findings.title: Security events and accounting events silently dropped at runtime
findings.evidence: E022: FailClosedSecurityHook and FailClosedSpine are stub implementations that log at ERROR level and drop the event. Comments acknowledge: 'Replace with a live SwarmEventBroadcaster once the security spine is operational' and 'Replace with a live accounting spine once the revenue spine is operational'.
findings.impact: Any on-chain security event (slash, dispute, custody violation, agent-law violation) is logged but never reaches an off-chain consumer. Audit trails and incident response are impossible without these spines. This affects slashing detection, dispute resolution, treasury accountability, and compliance.
findings.recommendation: Wire the swarm-api service (services/x3-swarm-api) to consume these events end-to-end before any public testnet. Add an integration test that emits a slash event and asserts it reaches the swarm-api consumer.

findings.title: mainnet-rc1 feature build is wired but unverified
findings.evidence: E016: mainnet-rc1 feature exists in both runtime and node Cargo.toml. CURRENT_MAINNET_STATUS.md states 'Node build w/ mainnet-rc1 — 🟡 Not verified — Pre-existing compile error in committed HEAD'.
findings.impact: Cannot ship the RC1 runtime WASM without first compiling the narrow pallet set. Without a successful WASM build, no srtool verification, no genesis ceremony, no public testnet.
findings.recommendation: Run `cargo build --release -p x3-chain-runtime --features mainnet-rc1 --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` and resolve the pre-existing compile error. Add this to CI as a required gate.
findings.evidence_quality: Inferred from CURRENT_MAINNET_STATUS.md (not re-verified in this audit because the WASM target requires additional setup)

findings.title: External bridge gateway production paths are untested audit-ready design only
findings.evidence: LAUNCH_SCOPE.md states: 'external-gateway: Compile-time compile_error! with mainnet-rc1 ... Code exists but is gated off by compile_error! + ExternalBridgesEnabled = false'. crates/x3-crosschain-gateway/src/lib.rs is 1285 lines of real implementation but is never executed in the mainnet-rc1 build.
findings.impact: External bridges (Ethereum, Solana, Bitcoin) are designed and typed but have no runtime evidence of correctness. The first time they execute will be when governance enables them — at which point any bug puts user funds at risk.
findings.recommendation: Run a regtest/integration suite that exercises the full deposit→proof→verification→mint and burn→release→withdrawal flow before governance enablement. Per BTC_FORTRESS_GATEWAY registry entry, regtest Bitcoin testing is 'SIM_TESTNET only — regtest Bitcoin, not mainnet'.

findings.title: production.json genesis contains dev seed accounts
file_refs: runtime/genesis-presets/production.json:6 dev accounts, 6B X3 endowment, system.code='0x', sudo=null
findings.evidence: E011: production.json uses Alice/Bob/Charlie/Dave/Eve/Ferdie accounts with 1B X3 each (6B total). system.code is '0x' (2 bytes — empty runtime blob). sudo key is null.
findings.impact: If a production launch accidentally uses this JSON without the chain_spec.rs guard, every well-known dev seed would be a validator with 1B X3. chain_spec.rs:125 assert_no_forbidden_live_seed() guards against the X3_DEV_SEED env var but the JSON file itself contains dev accounts.
findings.recommendation: Either: (a) remove dev accounts from production.json entirely, replacing with placeholders requiring explicit override, or (b) add a compile-time check that rejects construction of production_config when this JSON is used unmodified.

findings.title: x3-lang Python pipeline is MVP, Rust compiler is experimental
findings.evidence: x3-lang/README.md states: 'Python files: authoritative for the shipping intent DSL and MVP pipeline. Rust compiler work in crates/x3-compiler is experimental and not production-ready.'
findings.impact: The X3 language has two parallel implementations with unclear contract. Users cannot rely on either as production-stable. Compiler determinism invariant (LANG-COMPILE-001) is asserted but not validated against both implementations.
findings.recommendation: Pick one canonical implementation (likely Python for shipping intent DSL), freeze the other, and add end-to-end tests that compile the same .x3 source on both and compare bytecode hash.
findings.evidence_quality: Confirmed by static inspection of README
